title: Storytelling With Data
objective: After this lesson you will be able to structure findings as narratives (context, tension, resolution), annotate charts to guide reading, title with takeaways, and attach caveats without undermining conclusions.
why: Correct charts undecided change nothing: stakeholders fund narratives, not plots. Storytelling structures (situation → complication → resolution), annotated guidance (what to look at, in what order), takeaway titles (claims, checkable), and honest caveats (limits stated) convert analysis into decisions — the entire point of the previous nine lessons.

blocks.text: Every data story: **context** (what we sell, to whom, since when), **tension** (the cliff/gap/anomaly with numbers), **resolution** (recommended action with expected effect + caveats). Tension without context confuses; resolution without tension underwhelms. One story per presentation — three findings need three narratives or one ranked with explicit priority, never a data dump.

Charts don't self-narrate: **annotate** the cliff ('views→carts −78%'), the anomaly ('March spike = campaign X'), the comparison ('vs 55% benchmark'). Annotations order reading (look here, then here) and preempt misreads. Unannotated charts invite every wrong conclusion equally — guidance is kindness to busy readers.

blocks.caption: Story as data structure: claim, evidence pointers, bounds

blocks.text: **Takeaway titles** state conclusions ('Shoes drove Q3 growth') — checkable against the chart below, falsifiable by design. **Caveats** bound claims (samples, windows, methods) without undermining them: bounded confidence beats false precision. Stories without caveats invite the first skeptical question to demolish them; stated limits disarm it in advance.

blocks.title: Title the takeaway
blocks.note: Run it: argued+cited scores strong true; descriptive title with no numbers/caveats fails both. Titles argue (falsifiable), charts evidence (numbers), caveats bound — the complete contract.

items: Spine: context → tension (quantified) → resolution (action + expected effect)
Annotate reading paths (what/where/order); takeaway titles argue falsifiably
Caveats bound claims (samples/windows/methods) — stated limits disarm skeptics in advance

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice title scorer on both titles and map verdicts. (b) Write a takeaway title + two annotations + one caveat for the shoes/hats funnel finding. (c) State what makes a caveat strengthen rather than undermine a story.
hints: Verdicts: strong-true (argues + cited) vs false/false (describes nothing, evidences nothing).
Title argues ('Fix hats PDP first: 5.6% vs 25%'); annotations point (cliff, benchmark); caveat bounds (n, window).
Caveats strengthen by preempting the demolishing question: bounded confidence beats false precision; hidden limits detonate on discovery.
exercise.why: Title scoring (argue + cite), story units (claim + guidance + bounds), and caveat framing (preemption vs detonation) are the three storytelling judgments.
exercise.code: // Story-unit pattern: takeaway title + annotations + caveats, always together.

quiz.q: 'Sales by month' as a deck title. Upgrade?
options: Takeaway form ('Shoes drove Q3 growth') + numbers + caveats: argue falsifiably with evidence attached
quiz.explain: Descriptive titles abdicate interpretation; takeaway titles argue checkably. Claims invite verification — descriptions invite misreading.

options: Strengthen when stated upfront: bounded confidence preempts demolishing questions; hidden limits detonate on discovery
quiz.explain: Stated bounds disarm skeptics in advance. Concealed limits convert routine questions into credibility crises.

options: One narrative each (or one ranked with explicit priority): context → tension → resolution per story, never undifferentiated plots
quiz.explain: Stories need arcs: undifferentiated plots diffuse attention across unranked findings. Rank explicitly or narrate separately.

summary: Spine (context/tension/resolution), annotated paths, arguing titles, bounding caveats. Analysis becomes decisions through narrative discipline.
